identity.title: DR Tulu: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics for Deep Research

problem.claim: Train deep-research agents for open-ended, long-form, well-attributed answers.

gap.claim: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has mostly used easily verifiable short-form QA, limiting extension to realistic long-form research.

contributions.claim: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics (RLER), in which rubrics co-evolve with the policy model and incorporate information from search and contrasting responses.
DR Tulu-8B, an open model directly trained for open-ended, long-form deep research.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DR Tulu-8B as the first fully open model directly trained for open-ended, long-form deep research.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that DR Tulu-8B substantially outperforms existing open agents across four long-form benchmarks, averaging 15.6% over Tongyi DR.
The authors report that it matches or exceeds proprietary agents, averaging 0.7% over OpenAI DR, while being significantly smaller and 1000× cheaper per query than OpenAI DR.
The authors report that evolving rubrics enable more discriminative on-policy feedback and better fact checking.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep-research agents produce long-form answers through multi-step research and attribution.
Existing reinforcement-learning practice centers on short-form QA with easily verifiable rewards.
RLER co-evolves maintained rubrics with the policy, using newly searched information and contrasting responses.
The resulting DR Tulu-8B is evaluated across four science, healthcare, and general-domain benchmarks with reported performance and cost advantages.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links rubric maintenance to newly explored search information and contrasting model responses, then reports benchmark and cost comparisons for the resulting model.

lessons.interpretation: A research narrative can connect an adaptive feedback mechanism to both its information sources and downstream evaluation dimensions.
lessons.application: When presenting a training method, specify how feedback changes during training and evaluate capability, comparator-relative performance, and resource cost together.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when feedback is fixed or when resource measurements are unavailable or not comparable.

unknowns: The abstract does not define the benchmark metrics, aggregation method, or statistical uncertainty behind the reported percentage differences.
It does not specify the evaluation protocols, model sizes and costs used for comparison, or what conditions underlie the fact-checking claim.
